industry: b2b-services (civil / site engineering, planning and surveying)

opportunities.title: Fix the front door: working contact path, mobile-readable site, claimed Google profile
opportunities.problem: The firm's only enquiry path is a phone number, a fax number and a circa-2000s table form. The header email link points at a placeholder address, so it goes nowhere; the phone number is plain text with no tap-to-call; the layout has no viewport tag so the phone view is a shrunken desktop page; the Google listing shows a 'Claim this business' prompt with no hours and no photos. A civil-engineering practice selling to developers and municipalities is effectively unreachable and unreadable online.
evidence: Header email link is hard-coded to mailto:ourname@ouraddress.com instead of the firm's real address — every header contact click is dead (https://amertechengineering.com/)

Contact page offers only 757 Ridgewood Avenue, phone 732.828.3535, fax 732.249.0859 and a plain-field form with no project, parcel, municipality or deadline fields (https://amertechengineering.com/id5.html)

Site is Trellix Site Builder with no viewport meta tag, an '© 2011 – 2016' footer and a 'Ridgewod Avenue' header typo; phone view renders as an unreadable shrunken desktop page (https://amertechengineering.com/)

No JSON-LD, no meta description, page title is only the company name, robots.txt is an empty file and sitemap.xml returns 404 — nothing tells a search engine or an AI assistant what the firm does or which towns it serves (https://amertechengineering.com/robots.txt)

Google Maps panel shown in the earlier browser pass carried a 3.4 rating with no review count, 'Claim this business' and 'Add hours' prompts and no photos; the profile notes the Maps panel could not be re-loaded, so treat the rating as unverified (https://www.google.com/maps/search/Amertech+Engineering+North+Brunswick+NJ)
Navigation has no team, careers or staff page, so the firm has no page a PE or a municipal clerk can point to when checking who they are dealing with (https://amertechengineering.com/index.html)
opportunities.agent_design: Not an autonomous agent first — this is remediation the agents then stand on. Scope: (1) responsive rebuild of the six legacy pages around services and towns served, with a real tel: link, a corrected mailto, office hours, the correct 'Ridgewood' spelling and a plain-language service list; (2) a working enquiry form with server-side delivery, an autoreply and a ticket ID, plus file-upload for plans; (3) JSON-LD LocalBusiness/ProfessionalService markup, sitemap.xml and meta descriptions so assistants can read and quote the firm; (4) claim and complete the Google Business Profile (categories, hours, service area, project photos, licence line) with a small agent that watches for new reviews and drafts a reply for a human to send. Human approves every published page, listing change and review reply; nothing is auto-posted.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: The rebuild part is a web job, but the value comes from the wiring behind it: form → acknowledgement → routing, schema an AI assistant can actually parse, and a listing that stays correct. A DIY page builder reproduces the same dead mailto and the same unlabelled fields; keeping the intake path, listing and markup in sync needs ownership and monitoring, which is what a retainer buys.

impact_estimate.range: No defensible dollar figure; the measurable effect is removal of one confirmed dead contact route (the header email link), restoration of a usable phone layout and a form that returns an acknowledgement instead of silence. Expect 1–3 additional usable enquiries per month as an order-of-magnitude planning assumption, not a sourced number.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes the site currently receives some traffic (it is indexed and hosts the firm's only published service and project pages) and that at least a few enquiries per month fail today because of the broken mailto, the shrunken phone layout or the missing hours. No web-conversion benchmark for small civil-engineering firms was found in the industry brief or in search, so nothing is multiplied by a conversion rate. Because no sourced benchmark exists, this opportunity is scored on gap evidence and risk, not on revenue.

opportunities.pilot_scope: Two weeks: rebuilt responsive six-page site on a modern host with click-to-call, working email, hours and a form that acknowledges and files enquiries; claimed and completed Google profile with photos and correct categories; JSON-LD plus sitemap; a one-page before/after showing the phone-width rendering, the fixed mailto and the listing status.

opportunities.title: Developer-enquiry intake agent: qualify parcel, municipality, project type and deadline before a PE touches it
opportunities.problem: Enquiries arrive by phone, fax or a generic six-field form that captures name, company, mailing address, 'product/service' and 'best way to contact' — nothing about the parcel, block and lot, municipality, project type, submission deadline or attached plans. Senior time is spent extracting that by phone, and proposal writing is explicitly a licensed-engineer duty rather than a business-development role, so the most expensive person in the firm does the qualification.
evidence: Contact form fields are name, email, company, mailing address, product/service and contact method — no project type, parcel, municipality or deadline, and no acknowledgement or ticket ID (https://amertechengineering.com/id5.html)

The site markets feasibility studies, zoning analysis, concept plans and permits processing, i.e. work whose scoping questions (site, zone, use, unit count, submission date) are predictable and repeatable (https://amertechengineering.com/id4.html)

The Professional Civil Engineer posting makes 'prepare proposals' and leading engineers, technicians and administrative staff part of a licensed PE's job, 5–8 years experience with an NJ PE licence required — qualification work sits at the top of the wage scale (https://engineerjobs.io/amertech-engineering-inc)

Two different intake rhythms exist: recurring municipal agendas and deadlines plus one-off developer scoping, with expert testimony and board appearances to schedule (https://amertechengineering.com/id1.html)
No CRM, booking widget, chat or analytics tag anywhere in the page source, so there is no system of record for enquiries (https://amertechengineering.com/id5.html)
opportunities.agent_design: Event-driven agent behind the site form, a dedicated intake mailbox and a forwarded-call voicemail line. On each enquiry it parses the message, extracts municipality, block/lot or address, project type (subdivision, site plan, variance, stormwater, survey), unit or square-footage scale, desired submission date and any attachments, then looks up the parcel against NJ parcel and municipal zoning sources and drafts a triage sheet: what is needed, which approvals apply, likely fee drivers, and a suggested fee range from the firm's own historical fee schedule. It replies to the developer within minutes acknowledging receipt with a ticket ID and a short list of missing items, books a scoping call, and drops a structured record into a shared tracker. A human (PE or office manager) approves every fee range and every outbound scoping reply before it is sent; the agent never quotes a binding fee or signs anything.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: Requires persistent state across email, web form, voicemail and a parcel/municipal lookup, plus a per-client record, plus guardrails that stop a model from inventing a fee or a filing deadline. A chatbot subscription has no ticket state, no parcel lookups, no fee history and no audit trail of what was promised to a developer.

impact_estimate.range: $6,000–$15,000/yr of senior engineering time recovered, plus an unquantified reduction in enquiries lost to silence.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes 2–5 hours a week of PE-level time currently goes to enquiry triage, first responses and proposal scoping (upper end during proposal clusters). 48 working weeks × 96–240 hours at the NJ civil engineer median of $104,660 (~$50/hr base, ~$65/hr at a 1.3 loaded factor) gives roughly $6k–$15k. The labour-saving share is not assumed to be 100%: the agent drafts, a human still reviews. Peer-reviewed evidence that supports the drafting step is the preregistered professional-writing experiment (average 40% faster, 18% higher quality on mid-level writing tasks — a simulated-task study, not live client work) and the QJE 2025 support-desk rollout (+15% issues resolved per hour, larger for less-experienced staff). The industry brief's ACEC survey (self-reported, not measured) reports 68% of engineering firms expect AI could automate up to 29% of current tasks.

opportunities.pilot_scope: Three weeks: intake agent live on the web form and a dedicated mailbox; structured tracker with municipality, parcel, project type and deadline fields; 15–25 real enquiries processed with a PE approving every reply; a short reconciliation showing enquiries received, qualified, missing-information gaps and time per enquiry before and after.

opportunities.title: Municipal review-comment drafting agent grounded in each town's ordinance and the firm's own prior letters
opportunities.problem: The firm acts as municipal engineer and board reviewer for roughly ten central New Jersey towns, plus boards of education and utility authorities, and its plans are revised repeatedly through review cycles (Raritan Borough site plans revised April and August 2025, an Old Bridge subdivision plat in July 2025). Each cycle means reading an ordinance and a resubmitted plan set, drafting comment letters and reports, and tracking what was asked for last round — repetitive document work that lands on licensed engineers who must personally review and seal the output.
evidence: Firm lists municipal service for Monroe Township (35 years), Plainsboro (19), Cranbury (10), Clark (10+), plus South Brunswick, East Brunswick, Franklin, New Brunswick, Highland Park and Edison, and Boards of Education and Utility Authorities (https://amertechengineering.com/id1.html)

Public filings show routine revision cycles: Amertech-prepared Raritan Borough site plans dated 2024 and revised April 2025, exhibits revised August 2025, and a July 16, 2025 Old Bridge preliminary plat signed for the firm by a licensed PE (https://www.raritanboro.org/_Content/pdf/Lagrange-St-Traffic-Study.pdf)

Review-comment response and resubmission are a routine part of the workflow, evidenced by the same plans being re-dated across review rounds (https://files-backend.assets.thrillshare.com/documents/asset/uploaded_file/1690/Old_Bridge_Township/efb1aa61-7a66-4f28-81b2-85092620a9ba/CIS-dated-July-16%2C-2025.pdf?disposition=inline)

The site publishes no downloads, case studies or reports, so institutional knowledge (ordinance requirements, standard details, past comment language) sits with staff rather than in any tool (https://amertechengineering.com/id62.html)

Professional-accountability constraint: AI output must be reviewed and sealed by the responsible licensee, so the agent can draft and check but cannot sign (industry brief constraint on NCEES model rules and state board AI guidance) (https://www.acec.org/resource/new-acec-research-institute-report-finds-ai-is-transforming-engineering-by-accelerating-human-talent/)
opportunities.agent_design: A retrieval-grounded knowledge agent over a private index of: each client town's land-use ordinance and checklist, the firm's own prior comment letters and board reports, its standard details and stormwater templates, and the current application's plan set and prior review round. Triggered when a plan set or resubmission lands in a shared folder, it produces a completeness check against the town's checklist, a first-draft comment letter with each item tied to the ordinance section it cites, and a delta list of which prior comments were addressed, partly addressed or not addressed. Engineers edit in Word/PDF as they do today, and a named PE reviews and seals before anything goes to the board. All content stays in the firm's own repository; no client plan data leaves the firm's environment unredacted.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: Needs retrieval over dozens of town-specific ordinances and years of the firm's own comment letters, citation back to the exact section, document-in/document-out handling of large plan sets, and a private deployment because municipal review correspondence and developer plans are confidential. Off-the-shelf chatbots cannot cite an ordinance section reliably or keep one town's rules from leaking into another town's letter.

impact_estimate.range: $8,000–$25,000/yr of engineering time recovered across the review-letter workload.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes roughly 3–6 review letters or board reports a week across the municipal portfolio at 1–2 hours of drafting each (inference from the number of appointments and the visible revision cadence; the firm publishes no volumes). If a quarter of that drafting time is returned, 36–150 hours a year per engineer at ~$50/hr base ($104,660 NJ median) lands in the low thousands per engineer and $8k–$25k across a small team — deliberately below a full-FTE saving because the PE must still review and seal every letter. Supporting but self-reported industry evidence: ACEC 2025 reports 68% of firms think AI could automate up to 29% of tasks; the peer-reviewed Science 2023 experiment found 40% faster completion on mid-level professional writing tasks (simulated, 20–30 minute tasks).

opportunities.pilot_scope: Four weeks on one town and one live application: index that town's ordinance plus the firm's last 20 comment letters, run the agent on one resubmission, and deliver a completeness check, a drafted comment letter with ordinance citations and a prior-comment delta list, with a PE's edit distance from draft to final measured. No change to how letters are issued.

lead_score.rationale: Pain is well evidenced and visible from outside: a dead placeholder mailto in the site header, no tap-to-call, a 2016 non-responsive Trellix site, zero structured data, an empty robots.txt and a Google listing prompting 'Claim this business' — while the firm is demonstrably busy (2025 subdivision and site-plan filings, two 2026 engineering hires). Fit is high for G and A (both are squarely in the consultancy's lane and both rewrite an intake path that today is phone, fax and a legacy form) and good for C, which is the highest-value but hardest sell because a PE must seal every letter. Ability to pay is moderate: 26 people per the firm's own Form 5500 with ~$3.6M in plan assets, long-running municipal appointments and high project values, but it is a small owner-run practice with no published fee schedule and no evidence of an existing software budget — expect a modest first engagement, not a large one. Ease is good for the front-door work (two weeks, low ambiguity) and middling for the agent work since the firm has no CRM or portal to integrate with. Strategic value is high: the same front-door-plus-intake package sells to every civil/site engineering and surveying consultancy in central NJ, a segment with hundreds of near-identical legacy sites. No physical/edge (E) opportunity is proposed despite the profile's physical_signals: those describe a 3,400 sq ft 1962 office building, not a production, warehouse or fleet operation. There is no throughput, inventory, temperature or quality process on site for cameras or sensors to watch, and the firm's actual physical work (field survey, site visits at client parcels) is mobile and outside the office, so an E pilot would need hardware on land the firm does not own. That argues against E on evidence grounds rather than on preference. Evidence is not thin overall, but two parts are: the Google rating/claimed status could not be re-verified in the latest pass (treat 3.4 as unverified), and no decision-maker name is confirmed from the company's own pages.

best_evidence_signal: The header email link on the firm's own homepage is hard-coded to mailto:ourname@ouraddress.com and the phone number has no tel: link, on a Trellix site whose footer still reads '© 2011 – 2016' — https://amertechengineering.com/
